title: Article 136 — Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court

content.overview: Article 136 empowers the Supreme Court, in its discretion, to grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order in any cause or matter passed or made by any court or tribunal in the territory of India. This power does not apply to any judgment, determination, sentence or order passed or made by any court or tribunal constituted by or under any law relating to the Armed Forces.
content.glance: SC may grant special leave to appeal from any court or tribunal in India (except Armed Forces courts/tribunals). Discretionary plenary appellate power.
content.study:
Article 136 is a plenary, discretionary power:
- Special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order of any court or tribunal in India.
- Exception: courts or tribunals constituted by or under any law relating to the Armed Forces.
- Not a matter of right; the Supreme Court grants leave in its discretion.

It supplements the certificate-based appeals under Articles 132–134 and is a major pathway for appellate scrutiny.

Examination: discretionary; any court/tribunal (civil/criminal/other); Armed Forces exclusion; not a right of appeal.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Discretionary special leave to appeal.
2. From any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order of any court or tribunal in India.
3. Exception: Armed Forces courts/tribunals under law relating to the Armed Forces.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the special leave jurisdiction under Article 136?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 136, the Supreme Court may, in its discretion, grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order in any cause or matter passed or made by any court or tribunal in the territory of India. This power does not apply to judgments, determinations, sentences or orders of courts or tribunals constituted by or under any law relating to the Armed Forces.
